degree_type: Bachelor of Arts (B.A.) – 2 field degree program; Major Field
verification_status: Verified - retrieved directly from Albert-Ludwigs-Universität Freiburg's official Studiengangfinder (programme search tool at https://uni-freiburg.de/studium/studienangebot/), which loads its full current catalogue from the university's own structured JSON data endpoint (https://uni-freiburg.de/wp-json/study-search/v1/studies) in a single request returning all 348 programme records the university's system holds, of which 234 carry the 'currently admitting' status flag the site's own frontend uses to build its displayed '241 Studiengänge gefunden' listing (234 currently-admitting + 7 discontinued-but-still-listed 'Aufgehoben' programmes = 241; this research used only the 234 currently-admitting records, then excluded 6 further records that are Staatsexamen or pre-Bologna Magister/Kirchliches-Examen degrees, i.e. neither Bachelor's nor Master's, leaving 228 in scope), fetched and parsed directly by researcher on 2026-08-21 via the finder's own browser network requests (confirmed as a public unauthenticated GET endpoint, also independently re-fetched by direct HTTP request outside the browser). This record's programme name, degree type, subject-track designation, standard duration, faculty and subject-group classification, and language of instruction were taken directly from that structured field data. Language of instruction was independently spot-verified against this programme's own official detail page (see official_program_url, URL pattern confirmed by loading multiple sample IDs and matching programme name/degree/faculty against the structured record), which displays an explicit 'Unterrichtssprache' fact for every programme; spot checks included Sustainable Systems Engineering, where the English-named Bachelor's page explicitly states 'Unterrichtssprache: Deutsch' while the same-subject Master's page explicitly states 'Unterrichtssprache: Englisch', and Embedded Systems Engineering, where the Bachelor's is explicitly bilingual ('Deutsch und Englisch') while the Master's is purely English -- confirming the structured field is source-stated per programme rather than a name-based inference in either direction.
researcher_notes: Two-subject (2-Fächer) Bachelor's model: a full B.A. requires combining this subject as a Hauptfach (Major Field) with a second subject as Nebenfach (Minor Field), or vice versa. Freiburg does publish programme-specific admission-ordinance documents (Zulassungs-/Eignungsfeststellungssatzung) under each detail page's 'Satzungen' section, but typically with several superseded historical versions per programme, making identification of a single canonical current URL unreliable without dedicated per-page legal-document review; none was asserted here to avoid recording a wrong or stale version. campus/delivery_mode/international_eligible left null: no explicit statement of these was found on the structured record or the sampled detail pages (no distinct campus field exists in Freiburg's data; no explicit distance/blended-learning designation was found; admission text discusses non-EU-applicant admission quotas, which is an admissions-process detail, not a simple eligibility statement, so it was not converted into an international_eligible value).

This record's programme name, degree type, subject-track designation, standard duration, faculty and subject-group classification, and language of instruction were taken directly from that structured field data. Language of instruction was independently spot-verified against this programme's own official detail page (see official_program_url, URL pattern confirmed by loading multiple sample IDs and matching programme name/degree/faculty against the structured record), which displays an explicit 'Unterrichtssprache' fact for every programme; spot checks included Sustainable Systems Engineering, where the English-named Bachelor's page explicitly states 'Unterrichtssprache: Deutsch' while the same-subject Master's page explicitly states 'Unterrichtssprache: Englisch', and Embedded Systems Engineering, where the Bachelor's is explicitly bilingual ('Deutsch und Englisch') while the Master's is purely English -- confirming the structured field is source-stated per programme rather than a name-based inference in either direction.
